title: How Much Is a New Kitchen Renovation? UK Costs
description: How much is a new kitchen renovation in the UK? Explore typical costs for cabinets, worktops, appliances, installation and extras, plus budgeting tips.
keywords: cost of fitting a new kitchen
targetKeyword: how much is a new kitchen renovation

blocks.text: If you are asking how much a new kitchen renovation costs, the honest answer is that the price can vary considerably. As a rough UK guide, a straightforward replacement kitchen may typically cost around £8,000 to £15,000, while a mid-range renovation may typically fall between £15,000 and £30,000. A larger or higher-specification project, particularly one involving structural work or premium appliances, may cost more than £30,000. These are guide prices rather than fixed quotes: the room size, materials, layout and amount of building work will affect the final figure. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

For budgeting purposes, it helps to divide the project into three broad levels. A basic renovation might involve standard-sized cabinets, laminate worktops, a limited number of new appliances and minimal changes to the existing plumbing and electrics. A mid-range kitchen could include made-to-measure elements, higher-specification worktops, integrated appliances, improved lighting and some plastering or flooring. A premium renovation may involve bespoke cabinetry, stone or sintered-stone worktops, a completely new layout, structural alterations and more expensive appliances.

items: Basic kitchen renovation: as a rough guide, typically £8,000–£15,000, depending on the room and specification.
Mid-range kitchen renovation: as a rough guide, typically £15,000–£30,000, including more extensive fitting and higher-specification finishes.
Large or premium renovation: typically £30,000 and upwards, particularly where walls, windows, services or high-end materials are involved.

What is included in the cost?

The largest parts of the budget can include cabinets, worktops, appliances and labour. Cabinet prices depend on the number of units, storage accessories, door style and whether the units are flat-pack, rigid or bespoke. As a rough guide, cabinets may account for around £3,000–£12,000 or more. Worktops may range from around £500 for a simple laminate option to several thousand pounds for natural stone, quartz or other premium surfaces. The exact amount depends on the length, cut-outs, edging and installation requirements. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

items: Cabinets and storage: as a rough guide, approximately £3,000–£12,000-plus.
Worktops: as a rough guide, approximately £500–£5,000-plus, depending on the material and design.
Appliances: typically approximately £2,000–£10,000 for a full set, although keeping suitable existing appliances can reduce the total.
Installation and associated trades: this may cost several thousand pounds, depending on the complexity and duration of the work.

blocks.text: Common extras that can change the budget

A kitchen quotation may look affordable until associated work is included. Moving a sink, dishwasher, cooker or radiator can require changes to plumbing, electrics or gas arrangements. Removing a wall, widening a doorway or installing a roof lantern can add structural and design costs. Other possible extras include plastering, painting, new flooring, splashbacks, tiling, lighting, extractor installation, waste removal and making good after the old kitchen is removed.
Allow for the less visible work

Before comparing prices, check whether the quotation includes dismantling and disposal of the existing kitchen, preparation of walls and floors, fitting of appliances, electrical alterations, plumbing, tiling and final connections. Also ask whether VAT is included. If the old room reveals damaged plaster, uneven floors, outdated wiring or leaking pipework, remedial work may be necessary before the new units can be installed. Consider setting aside a contingency for unexpected work, but discuss an appropriate allowance with your contractor because the amount will vary by project.
How to plan a more accurate kitchen budget

Start with a measured plan rather than choosing products at random. Record the room dimensions, window and door positions, ceiling height, existing service locations and any appliances you intend to retain. Then decide which elements matter most to you. For example, you may prefer to spend more on durable worktops and storage while choosing standard cabinet doors, or invest in appliances while keeping the existing layout. Keeping plumbing and electrical points in broadly the same positions can reduce the amount of alteration work needed, although suitability should be checked on site.

items: Create a complete list of cabinets, panels, handles, worktops, appliances and accessories before requesting prices.
Ask for labour, delivery, disposal, preparation, VAT and finishing work to be shown separately.
Confirm who is responsible for appliance connections, tiling, flooring, decorating and waste removal.
Obtain comparable written quotations based on the same specification, not just similar-looking cabinet prices.
Keep a contingency for hidden defects and choose appliances and finishes before the final order is placed.

Questions to ask before accepting a quotation

Ask whether the quote is based on a fixed design and specification, and what happens if you change a product after ordering. Check the expected start date, project duration, payment stages, protection of adjoining rooms and arrangements for water, cooking and refrigeration while the work is under way. A detailed quote should make clear what is included and excluded, so you can compare the full scope of each option rather than choosing the lowest headline figure. Every kitchen is different, so a measured survey and itemised quotation are generally more useful than a generic online calculator.

faq.q: How much does a new kitchen renovation cost in the UK?
faq.a: As a rough guide, a new kitchen renovation may typically cost £8,000–£15,000 at the simpler end, £15,000–£30,000 for a mid-range project, or £30,000-plus for a larger premium renovation. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: What is the most expensive part of a kitchen renovation?
faq.a: Cabinets, worktops, appliances and installation can make up a substantial part of the cost. Structural changes, moving services and premium materials can increase the budget further.

faq.q: Can I reduce the cost of a new kitchen renovation?
faq.a: Keeping the existing layout, retaining suitable appliances, choosing standard cabinet sizes and comparing itemised quotations can help control costs. Do not reduce the budget by overlooking necessary electrical, plumbing or preparation work.

faq.q: Does a kitchen renovation quote include appliances and fitting?
faq.a: Not always. Ask whether the quotation includes appliances, delivery, installation, connections, old-kitchen removal, waste disposal, VAT, tiling, flooring and decorating before comparing prices.

faq.q: How much contingency should I allow for a kitchen renovation?
faq.a: Consider allowing a contingency for unexpected work, particularly where the condition of the room is uncertain. The appropriate amount depends on the age and condition of the room and the extent of the renovation.
